name: Fighter
description: Fighters share an unparalleled mastery with weapons and armor, and a thorough knowledge of the skills of combat. They are well acquainted with death, both meting it out and staring it defiantly in the face.

features.name: Fighter Proficiencies
features.description:
**Armor**

Light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, shields

**Weapons**

Simple weapons, martial weapons

**Skills**

Choose 2 from: Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, Survival

features.name: Fighting Style
features.description: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty.

options.name: Archery
options.description: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.
options.snippet: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

options.name: Defense
options.description: While you are wearing armor, your Absorb value increases by 1, even if the armor does not normally have Absorb.
options.snippet: While you are wearing armor, your Absorb increases by 1.

options.name: Dueling
options.description: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
options.snippet: When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

options.name: Great Weapon Fighting
options.description: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.
options.snippet: When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll.

options.name: Protection
options.description: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.
options.snippet: When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

options.name: Dual Wielding
options.description: You can use two-weapon fighting as long as one of the weapons you are holding has the Light property.
options.snippet: You can use two-weapon fighting as long as one of the weapons you are holding has the Light property.

options.name: Blind Fighting
options.description: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.
options.snippet: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

options.name: Interception
options.description: When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see is attacked, you can use your reaction to shift the target of the attack to be yourself.
options.snippet: When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see is attacked, you can use your reaction to shift the target of the attack to be yourself.

options.name: Unarmed Fighting
options.description: Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. When you succeed a Shove or Grapple attack against a creature, they take damage equal to your Strength modifier.
options.snippet: Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. When you succeed a Shove or Grapple attack against a creature, they take damage equal to your Strength modifier.

features.name: Martial Prowess
features.description:
Your training as a soldier or warrior has imparted on you various techniques to utilize against your foes. You know two Prowesses from the Fighter prowess list.

**Prowesses Known**

The Fighter table shows how many Prowesses you know at 1st level and higher. When you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Martial Prowesses you know and replace it with another Prowess from the Fighter prowess list.

**Prowess Ability**

Strength or Dexterity, whichever is higher, is your Prowess ability for your fighter prowesses, as the power of your abilities relies on your physical capacity. You use your Strength or Dexterity whenever a prowess refers to your prowess ability. In addition, you use your Strength or Dexterity modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a fighter Prowess you use.

**Prowess save DC**

Your Prowess save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier
features.snippet: Your training as a soldier or warrior has imparted on you various techniques to utilize against your foes. You know two Prowesses from the Fighter prowess list.

features.name: Warrior’s Grit
features.description: Starting at 2nd level, you can make your abilities more potent. When a creature makes a saving throw against your Prowess save DC and succeeds, you can take a Stress to force them to reroll the die.
features.snippet: You can make your abilities more potent. When a creature makes a saving throw against your Prowess save DC and succeeds, you can take a Stress to force them to reroll the die.

features.name: Trait Improvement
features.description:
When you reach 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can improve upon one of your traits listed below. You have the following choices:

- Gain an additional Stress Slot
- Gain a +1 bonus to a Saving Throw
- Gain a +2 bonus to your Initiative
- Gain proficiency in a skill, tool, or language. This option may only be chosen twice.

features.name: Martial Archetype
features.description:
At 1st level, you choose a domain shaped by your choice of Deity and the gifts they grant you. Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Channel Divinity when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.

**Domain Spells**

Each domain has a list of spells-its domain spells that you gain at the cleric levels noted in the domain description. Once you gain a domain spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.

If you have a domain spell that doesn't appear on the cleric spell list, the spell is nonetheless a cleric spell for you.
